newsitem.title: morocco: Arafat in Rabat for meeting with U.S. envoy Ross.
newsitem.headline: Arafat in Rabat for meeting with U.S. envoy Ross.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in the Moroccan capital Rabat where he was to meet on Thursday with U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross on the growing crisis in Israeli-Palestinian peacemaking.

Ross, who arrived in Rabat on Wednesday evening, was sent by U.S. President Bill Clinton with messages to Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to try to stop Israeli-Palestinian violence and restart peace talks.

"There is a message with Dennis Ross from President Clinton... We shall see," Arafat told reporters on arrival at Rabat airport. Ross was due to leave Morocco for Israel later on Thursday where he would hold similar talks with Netanyahu.

The crisis erupted when Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem earlier this month. Clashes broke out afterwards and last Friday, a Palestinian suicide bomber killed three Israeli women at a Tel Aviv cafe.
Ross also discussed the crisis with King Hassan of Morocco on Wednesday night ahead of a meeting of the Jerusalem Committee on Thursday to discuss ways to counter Israeli policies.

"President Clinton has sent me out here to have a chance to speak to Chairman Arafat. Being here in Morocco is an opportunity to meet his majesty King Hassan who is a strong supporter of the peace process and whose advice and counsel are often sought by President Clinton," Ross told Reuters.
Ross said he would return to Washington by the weekend to report to Clinton on his discussions so the "president can decide what the next proper move should be."
Fifteen foreign ministers of Islamic countries arrived in Rabat to attend the Jerusalem Committee meeting, which was called by King Hassan following Israel's latest settlement project.
The Jerusalem Committee, headed by King Hassan, was set up by an Islamic Conference Organisation summit in 1975 with the aim of preventing Israel from making any demographic changes to Jerusalem.
